--- Page 1 (Beckerman_27a) --- Dear Folks and Ruth: Today's my Sunday turn to work so will take opportunity of getting off a few letters. You remember some time ago I told you that we rotate Sunday duty so that detail has finally come around to me for the first time in about four months. Haven't heard from you this week but suppose that the letter will be coming in tomorrow. These weeks sure do fly by and before I know it why its time to write again. Some of the fellows around here have left to go home to the states and naturally we had the usual farewell parties. Of course they've been here a long time now. Everything going along in the usual tip top shape. got a letter from Sam B. and for the first time I saw a picture. He's a good looking husky kid. Also heard from Harry and finally that long overdue letter from Abe. Everybody doing OK. We are quite lucky in that respect. I feel like a sight seeing guide by now. Ladies and gents; more scenic views. Enclosed there's a group of shots of Aust soldiers on parade. That's one thing this country is really proud of--their diggers(soldiers). They are supposed to be some of the top notch fighters in the world. You should see these fellows--they are a tough lot. I'll have a lot of stories about them for you. Then there's an interesting shot of a mounted policeman we took in Sidney last year. One view of the train enroute to Brisbane. You've heard of all the gasoline saving devices that have been dreamed up because of gasoline shortages. Well I think these people beat them all. Hardly a civilian car is to be seen that doesn't have a sort of weird contraption for saving gas. The of the types are shown on the enclosed shots. Notice the kind of to the rear of the bus; that's a charcoal burner and is supposed to be very efficient. Then there's a side and front gadget. I couldn't find out what it was about. --- Page 2 (Beckerman_27b) --- That's actually nothing more than ordinary cooking gas which is used in lieu of gasoline. You recall I often have told you about Gregory Terrace. I have a shot that really shows the prettiness of the place. This shot was taken from Victoria Park where all the US Army office bldgs are. We work there too. This huge golf course separates the Office Bldgs from the Officers quarters. The bldg right in the center (under dot) is the Officers Club and all the little white structures surrounding it & are the houses in which we live. And so we come to the end of another tour. And the end of another letter which I hope finds you all well, and happy. The news of the President's death came as a shocking blow to everyone as it reached us on the 14th. Tributes are everywhere to this greatest man. We are hoping that his efforts will be carried on. [illegible]
